items.title: feat(id): tooltip-mode, pin and minimize state machine for cursors (#1790 slice 1)
items.body: Slice 1 of 3 for #1790 (per the split suggested on the issue's verified park notes): the pure state machine in `pkgs/id/web/src/cursor-utils.ts`, with tests. This PR does **not** close #1790 — slices 2 (cursors.ts wiring + UI toggle) and 3 (client/server lifecycle logging + liveness-based fade) remain on task 14115. ## What lands - `TooltipMode` (`full` / `minimal` / `hidden`) + `nextTooltipMode` toggle cycle. - `resolveTooltipDisplay` — precedence oracle is the #1790 text: hidden mode hides unpinned cursors (pinned exempt), an explicit per-cursor minimize hides in any mode, the click-to-enlarge chain overrides the resting display, minimal mode shows the tooltip only at hover >= 1s (`HOVER_TOOLTIP_DELAY_MS`), full mode shows the tooltip. - Click-to-enlarge revert chain: `getEnlargeStage` — big -> tooltip -> minimal, one 1s step each (`ENLARGE_STEP_MS`); clock skew reads as just-enlarged. - Per-cursor display state: immutable `setCursorPinned` / `setCursorMinimized` map updates and `partitionCursorsByMinimized` producing the visible set and the minimize/restore list. ## Tests (oracle: #1790 settled scope text) - New `pkgs/id/web/src/cursor-tooltip-state.test.ts`: 20 tests — mode cycle, enlarge-stage boundaries (0 / 999 / 1000 / 1999 / 2000 ms, skew), hover threshold boundary (999 / 1000 ms), pinned exemption, minimize precedence, partition order. - `bunx vitest run src/cursor-tooltip-state.test.ts src/cursor-utils.test.ts` — 98 passed. `bunx tsc --noEmit` — clean. - Full web suite: 705 passed, 1 failed — `search-panel.test.ts` aria-label expectation, verified pre-existing on clean `main` (same failure with this change stashed); unrelated to cursors. ## Liveness note (acceptance item, documented per #1790) Verified by prior lanes and carried here: fade age is currently `now - lastUpdate`, and `lastUpdate` refreshes on cursor *position* updates, not on websocket pong/activity — inactivity is NOT yet liveness-based. Fixing that is slice 3 scope (with the lifecycle logging), not this PR. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Cursor tooltip display now supports full, minimal, and hidden modes, with hover-based timing and staged cursor enlargement. * Cursors can be pinned to keep them visible or explicitly minimized. * **Tests** * Added coverage for tooltip timing and modes, pinning and minimization, and cursor ordering.

items.title: feat(id): cursor tooltip modes/pin/minimize wiring + lifecycle logging (#1790 slices 2+3)
items.body: Slices 2+3 of #1790 (slice 1, the pure state machine, landed via PR #7993). Closes the remaining acceptance on #1790. ## Slice 2 — wiring in `pkgs/id/web/src/cursors.ts` - Per-view tooltip mode (`full` / `minimal` / `hidden`, default `full`) resolved for every remote cursor through slice 1's `resolveTooltipDisplay`; hidden/minimized cursors stay tracked in plugin state but render nothing. - Standalone cursors: `minimal` renders the cursor line only; a label click starts the click-to-enlarge chain (big → tooltip → minimal, 1s steps via `getEnlargeStage`), and clicking a rested chain clears it. The enlarged ("big") label carries **pin/unpin** and **minimize** buttons (pin exempts the cursor from hidden mode). - Merged bars: minimal segments render name-less, big segments are marked, segments are click-to-enlarge too. Widget/cluster keys include the resolved display so the 1s refresh tick re-renders chain steps and hover tooltips. - Chrome: the plugin view mounts a `Cursors: ` toggle button (cycles full → minimal → hidden) plus one **Restore** button per minimized cursor — the minimize/restore list for all modes, fed by `partitionCursorsByMinimized`. - Exported `setCursorTooltipMode` / `getCursorTooltipMode` for embedders/tests. ## Slice 3 — lifecycle logging - Client (`cursors.ts` + pure helpers in `cursor-utils.ts`): `[cursor-lifecycle]` lines for **first-inactive** (age ≥ FADE_START_MS) and **minimum-reached** (≥ FADE_END_MS), logged once per inactive stretch, **removed** on removal, and **hover / unhover** from the label hover handlers. - Server (`pkgs/id/src/web/collab.rs`): `[cursor-lifecycle] first-seen` when a client_id enters the cursor map, and the 5-minute disconnect removal now logs as `[cursor-lifecycle] removed`. ## Liveness verification (issue acceptance) Inactivity is **connection-liveness based, not pointer-idleness based**: the server (`collab.rs`) pings every 30s and closes the socket after a 30-minute pong timeout; a connected client's cursor stays in the server map (it is only marked disconnected on socket close and removed 5 minutes later), and joining clients receive it with `idleSecs`. Client-side, cursor age is time since the last relayed cursor frame for that peer (`lastUpdate`, fed by websocket CURSOR frames / Init), never local pointer events; removal arrives as the server's CURSOR_REMOVE broadcast. No code in either path reads pointer-idle state. ## Tests - `bunx vitest run` (pkgs/id/web): cursor-tooltip-state + cursor-utils + collab = 127/127 pass, including 4 new lifecycle tests; full suite 710 passed / 9 skipped with **one pre-existing failure** in `search-panel.test.ts` (role=search aria-label) that fails identically on clean main — filed as #8012. - `bunx tsc --noEmit`: clean. `cargo check --lib` (pkgs/id): passes. 🤖 Queue worker lane code-w, task 14115. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: fix(mcpx): fieldInMessage token-boundary matching with quote preference (#1646)
items.body: Implements the matching contract pinned by triage task 1790 on #1646 (queue task 4083). ## What changed `fieldInMessage` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/diagnose/diagnose.go`) no longer bare-substring-matches prop names: 1. **Token rule** — a prop counts as named only as a standalone token (neighbouring chars are not ASCII letter/digit/`_`; message ends count as boundaries). `valid` inside `invalid` and `name` inside `unnamed` no longer blame fields the server never named. 2. **Quote preference** — an occurrence wrapped in matching `"…"`, `…` or `` `…` `` outranks a bare-token occurrence; longest name wins within the same class (preserves the `id` vs `user_id` disambiguation). 3. Case-sensitive as before; no separator folding (`user-id` does not name `user_id` — tested in isolation). 4. No token match → empty → the existing generic diagnostic fall-through. ## Tests New regression tests in `diagnose_test.go` covering BUG-A (`id` in `invalid`), BUG-B (`name` in `unnamed`), BUG-C (`valid` substring vs the genuinely named `id`, bare and quoted), plus the pinned controls: quoted `"query"`, `argument 'x'`, `x is required`, quote-beats-length, longest-within-class, hyphen boundary, no-folding, case sensitivity. - `go test ./internal/diagnose/` — pass on the laptop worktree (gofmt + `go vet` clean); full verification in CI per fleet policy. Closes the implementation for #1646 once merged; issue stays open until CI + review complete. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: Update Rust crate rand to v0.9.3 [SECURITY]
items.body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [rand](https://rust-random.github.io/book) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand)) | dependencies | minor | `0.8.5` → `0.9.0` |
| [rand](https://rust-random.github.io/book) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand)) | dependencies | patch | `0.9.2` → `0.9.3` |
| [rand](https://rust-random.github.io/book) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand)) | dependencies | minor | `0.8.5` → `0.9.3` |

---

### Rand is unsound with a custom logger using rand::rng()
[GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
It has been reported (by @​lopopolo) that the `rand` library is [unsound](https://rust-lang.github.io/unsafe-code-guidelines/glossary.html#soundness-of-code--of-a-library) (i.e. that safe code using the public API can cause Undefined Behaviour) when all the following conditions are met:

- The `log` and `thread_rng` features are enabled
- A [custom logger](https://docs.rs/log/latest/log/#implementing-a-logger) is defined
- The custom logger accesses `rand::rng()` (previously `rand::thread_rng()`) and calls any `TryRng` (previously `RngCore`) methods on `ThreadRng`
- The `ThreadRng` (attempts to) reseed while called from the custom logger (this happens every 64 kB of generated data)
- Trace-level logging is enabled or warn-level logging is enabled and the random source (the `getrandom` crate) is unable to provide a new seed

`TryRng` (previously `RngCore`) methods for `ThreadRng` use `unsafe` code to cast `*mut BlockRng<ReseedingCore>` to `&mut BlockRng<ReseedingCore>`. When all the above conditions are met this results in an aliased mutable reference, violating the Stacked Borrows rules. Miri is able to detect this violation in sample code. Since construction of [aliased mutable references is Undefined Behaviour](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/nomicon/references.html), the behaviour of optimized builds is hard to predict.

#### Severity
Low

#### References
- [https://github.com/rust-random/rand/pull/1763](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/pull/1763)
- [https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0097.html](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0097.html)
- [https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc)

This data is provided by the [GitHub Advisory Database](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc) ([CC-BY 4.0](https://redirect.github.com/github/advisory-database/blob/main/LICENSE.md)).
</details>

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>rust-random/rand (rand)</summary>

### [`v0.9.3`](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/releases/tag/0.9.3)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/compare/0.9.2...0.9.3)

This release back-ports a fix from v0.10. See also \[[#​1763](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/issues/1763)].

##### Changes

- Deprecate feature `log` ([#​1764](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/issues/1764))
- Replace usages of `doc_auto_cfg` ([#​1764](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/issues/1764))

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/rust-random/rand/compare/0.9.2...0.9.3>

### [`v0.9.2`](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#092---2025-07-20)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/compare/0.9.1...0.9.2)

##### Deprecated

- Deprecate `rand::rngs::mock` module and `StepRng` generator (\[[#​1634](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/issues/1634)])

##### Additions

- Enable `WeightedIndex<usize>` (de)serialization (\[[#​1646](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/issues/1646)])

### [`v0.9.1`](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#091---2025-04-17)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/compare/0.9.0...0.9.1)

##### Security and unsafe

- Revise "not a crypto library" policy again ([#​1565])
- Remove `zerocopy` dependency from `rand` ([#​1579])

##### Fixes

- Fix feature `simd_support` for recent nightly rust ([#​1586])

##### Changes

- Allow `fn rand::seq::index::sample_weighted` and `fn IndexedRandom::choose_multiple_weighted` to return fewer than `amount` results ([#​1623]), reverting an undocumented change (\[[#​1382](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/issues/1382)]) to the previous release.

##### Additions

- Add `rand::distr::Alphabetic` distribution. ([#​1587])
- Re-export `rand_core` ([#​1604])

### [`v0.9.0`](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#090---2025-01-27)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/compare/0.8.8...0.9.0)

##### Security and unsafe

- Policy: "rand is not a crypto library" ([#​1514])
- Remove fork-protection from `ReseedingRng` and `ThreadRng`. Instead, it is recommended to call `ThreadRng::reseed` on fork. ([#​1379])
- Use `zerocopy` to replace some `unsafe` code ([#​1349], [#​1393], [#​1446], [#​1502])

##### Dependencies

- Bump the MSRV to 1.63.0 ([#​1207], [#​1246], [#​1269], [#​1341], [#​1416], [#​1536]); note that 1.60.0 may work for dependents when using `--ignore-rust-version`
- Update to `rand_core` v0.9.0 ([#​1558])

##### Features

- Support `std` feature without `getrandom` or `rand_chacha` ([#​1354])
- Enable feature `small_rng` by default ([#​1455])
- Remove implicit feature `rand_chacha`; use `std_rng` instead. ([#​1473])
- Rename feature `serde1` to `serde` ([#​1477])
- Rename feature `getrandom` to `os_rng` ([#​1537])
- Add feature `thread_rng` ([#​1547])

##### API changes: rand_core traits

- Add fn `RngCore::read_adapter` implementing `std::io::Read` ([#​1267])
- Add trait `CryptoBlockRng: BlockRngCore`; make `trait CryptoRng: RngCore` ([#​1273])
- Add traits `TryRngCore`, `TryCryptoRng` ([#​1424], [#​1499])
- Rename `fn SeedableRng::from_rng` -> `try_from_rng` and add infallible variant `fn from_rng` ([#​1424])
- Rename `fn SeedableRng::from_entropy` -> `from_os_rng` and add fallible variant `fn try_from_os_rng` ([#​1424])
- Add bounds `Clone` and `AsRef` to associated type `SeedableRng::Seed` ([#​1491])

##### API changes: Rng trait and top-level fns

- Rename fn `rand::thread_rng()` to `rand::rng()` and remove from the prelude ([#​1506])
- Remove fn `rand::random()` from the prelude ([#​1506])
- Add top-level fns `random_iter`, `random_range`, `random_bool`, `random_ratio`, `fill` ([#​1488])
- Re-introduce fn `Rng::gen_iter` as `random_iter` ([#​1305], [#​1500])
- Rename fn `Rng::gen` to `random` to avoid conflict with the new `gen` keyword in Rust 2024 ([#​1438])
- Rename fns `Rng::gen_range` to `random_range`, `gen_bool` to `random_bool`, `gen_ratio` to `random_ratio` ([#​1505])
- Annotate panicking methods with `#[track_caller]` ([#​1442], [#​1447])

##### API changes: RNGs

- Fix `<SmallRng as SeedableRng>::Seed` size to 256 bits ([#​1455])
- Remove first parameter (`rng`) of `ReseedingRng::new` ([#​1533])

##### API changes: Sequences

- Split trait `SliceRandom` into `IndexedRandom`, `IndexedMutRandom`, `SliceRandom` ([#​1382])
- Add `IndexedRandom::choose_multiple_array`, `index::sample_array` ([#​1453], [#​1469])

##### API changes: Distributions: renames

- Rename module `rand::distributions` to `rand::distr` ([#​1470])
- Rename distribution `Standard` to `StandardUniform` ([#​1526])
- Move `distr::Slice` -> `distr::slice::Choose`, `distr::EmptySlice` -> `distr::slice::Empty` ([#​1548])
- Rename trait `distr::DistString` -> `distr::SampleString` ([#​1548])
- Rename `distr::DistIter` -> `distr::Iter`, `distr::DistMap` -> `distr::Map` ([#​1548])

##### API changes: Distributions

- Relax `Sized` bound on `Distribution<T> for &D` ([#​1278])
- Remove impl of `Distribution<Option<T>>` for `StandardUniform` ([#​1526])
- Let distribution `StandardUniform` support all `NonZero*` types ([#​1332])
- Fns `{Uniform, UniformSampler}::{new, new_inclusive}` return a `Result` (instead of potentially panicking) ([#​1229])
- Distribution `Uniform` implements `TryFrom` instead of `From` for ranges ([#​1229])
- Add `UniformUsize` ([#​1487])
- Remove support for generating `isize` and `usize` values with `StandardUniform`, `Uniform` (except via `UniformUsize`) and `Fill` and usage as a `WeightedAliasIndex` weight ([#​1487])
- Add impl `DistString` for distributions `Slice<char>` and `Uniform<char>` ([#​1315])
- Add fn `Slice::num_choices` ([#​1402])
- Add fn `p()` for distribution `Bernoulli` to access probability ([#​1481])

##### API changes: Weighted distributions

- Add `pub` module `rand::distr::weighted`, moving `WeightedIndex` there ([#​1548])
- Add trait `weighted::Weight`, allowing `WeightedIndex` to trap overflow ([#​1353])
- Add fns `weight, weights, total_weight` to distribution `WeightedIndex` ([#​1420])
- Rename enum `WeightedError` to `weighted::Error`, revising variants ([#​1382]) and mark as `#[non_exhaustive]` ([#​1480])

##### API changes: SIMD

- Switch to `std::simd`, expand SIMD & docs ([#​1239])

##### Reproducibility-breaking changes

- Make `ReseedingRng::reseed` discard remaining data from the last block generated ([#​1379])
- Change fn `SmallRng::seed_from_u64` implementation ([#​1203])
- Allow `UniformFloat::new` samples and `UniformFloat::sample_single` to yield `high` ([#​1462])
- Fix portability of distribution `Slice` ([#​1469])
- Make `Uniform` for `usize` portable via `UniformUsize` ([#​1487])
- Fix `IndexdRandom::choose_multiple_weighted` for very small seeds and optimize for large input length / low memory ([#​1530])

##### Reproducibility-breaking optimisations

- Optimize fn `sample_floyd`, affecting output of `rand::seq::index::sample` and `rand::seq::SliceRandom::choose_multiple` ([#​1277])
- New, faster algorithms for `IteratorRandom::choose` and `choose_stable` ([#​1268])
- New, faster algorithms for `SliceRandom::shuffle` and `partial_shuffle` ([#​1272])
- Optimize distribution `Uniform`: use Canon's method (single sampling) / Lemire's method (distribution sampling) for faster sampling (breaks value stability; [#​1287])
- Optimize fn `sample_single_inclusive` for floats (+\~20% perf) ([#​1289])

##### Other optimisations

- Improve `SmallRng` initialization performance ([#​1482])
- Optimise SIMD widening multiply ([#​1247])

##### Other

- Add `Cargo.lock.msrv` file ([#​1275])
- Reformat with `rustfmt` and enforce ([#​1448])
- Apply Clippy suggestions and enforce ([#​1448], [#​1474])
- Move all benchmarks to new `benches` crate ([#​1329], [#​1439]) and migrate to Criterion ([#​1490])

##### Documentation

- Improve `ThreadRng` related docs ([#​1257])
- Docs: enable experimental `--generate-link-to-definition` feature ([#​1327])
- Better doc of crate features, use `doc_auto_cfg` ([#​1411], [#​1450])

v0.23.2

This is the last v0 release, we are moving to v1!!

More details coming soon 👀

What's Changed

  • Implementing Parity-aware BPE by @​cimeister in huggingface/tokenizers#1974

New Contributors

  • @​eunseo9311 made their first contribution in huggingface/tokenizers#2074
  • @​cimeister made their first contribution in huggingface/tokenizers#1974

Full Changelog: https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers/compare/v0.23.1...v0.23.2

Release v0.23.1

TL;DR

tokenizers 0.23.1 is the first proper stable release in the 0.23 line — 0.23.0 only ever shipped as rc0 because the release pipeline itself was broken (Node side hadn't shipped multi-platform binaries since 2023, Python side was on pyo3 0.27 without free-threaded support). 0.23.1 is the version where everything actually goes out the door together: full Node multi-platform wheels for the first time in years, Python 3.14 (regular and free-threaded 3.14t), full type hints for every Python class, and a stack of measurable perf wins on the BPE / added-vocab hot paths.

There is no functional 0.23.0 published — we tag 0.23.1 directly so users don't accidentally pull a never-shipped version.

🚨 Breaking changes

  • Drop Python 3.9 (#1952) — requires-python = ">=3.10"; 3.9 users stay on 0.22.x.
  • add_tokens normalizes content at insertion (#1995) — re-saved tokenizer.json may differ in the added_tokens block. Existing files load unchanged.
  • Type stubs are precise (#1928, #1997) — methods that returned Any now return real types; mypy --strict may surface previously-hidden errors. Stub layout also moved from tokenizers/<sub>/__init__.pyi to tokenizers/<sub>.pyi. This breaks the surface of some of the processors like RobertaProcessign's __init__ .
  • 3.14t-only: setters/getters return PyResult<T> because of Arc<RwLock<Tokenizer>>; a poisoned lock surfaces as PyException instead of a panic.

Changelog

Sourced from base64's changelog.

0.23.1

  • Make the tests build again on non-SIMD architectures

0.23.0

  • Added more consts for preconfigured configs and engines
  • Make DecodeError::InvalidLastSymbol more clear by including the decoded value
  • Added SIMD-accelerated engines behind the default-on simd-unsafe feature: Simd picks the best instruction set at runtime (AVX2 on x86_64, NEON on aarch64) and falls back to the scalar GeneralPurpose engine, while Avx2 and Neon target one instruction set with no runtime detection and work in no_std. The engines support the standard and URL-safe alphabets.
  • Update MSRV to 1.71.0
  • Add support for custom padding symbols

items.title: mcpx: cap returned exec stdout at exec.maxOutputBytes (CODE-16 of #1937)
items.body: Implements **CODE-16 only** of #1937 (queue task 3234). Part of #1937 — does **not** close it: slices 2 (CODE-19+CODE-30) and 3 (CODE-35+CODE-36) remain on the issue. ## What Returned stdout from an mcpx exec run is now capped at a documented setting, applied once at the **execsvc Result boundary** (end of `Service.Run`), so the CLI, `/v1/exec` and the MCP tool all return the same capped stdout. - New setting **`exec.maxOutputBytes`** (settings registry, KindBytes, ScopeCall, default `64KiB`); `defaults.json` gains `exec.stdoutLimit: 65536` and `defaults.ExecStdoutLimit`, following the existing `stderrLimit` pattern. - Wired into `execsvc.Limits.StdoutLimit` by both service builders: daemon `ExecService()` and CLI `localService()`. - Over the cap: head kept (cut backs off to a UTF-8 boundary), returned string never exceeds the cap, ends with a marker naming kept/total/**dropped** bytes, and `Result.StdoutTruncated` (`stdoutTruncated`) is set. Truncation is visible, never silent. - Under / exactly at the cap: byte-identical to before. `0` disables the cap. - Internal consumers (the JSON answer parse, hooks) still work on the full text; full output is unchanged wherever a full record already exists (run record / artifacts). ## Docs - CODE-16 row + section in `docs/compare/register/code-mode.md` updated to the as-built state. - `docs/configuration.md` regenerated via the settings test `-update` (diff adds only this setting). ## Deliberate pin raise `EffectExemptionPin` 182 → 183 for `exec.maxOutputBytes`, with the same call-scoped-exec exemption rationale as `exec.timeout`. Recorded here per the pin rule in `effect_test.go`. ## Tests - New `internal/execsvc/stdout_limit_test.go`: over-cap → capped + marker naming dropped bytes; under-cap and exact-cap → byte-identical; 0 disables; UTF-8 boundary. - Laptop: `go test ./internal/execsvc/` **passes**. `./internal/settings/` and `./internal/defaults/` retain exactly the clean-main pre-existing guard failures (verified by stash comparison: docs/effect drift from the `model.*` settings, e.g. `TestTheEnvironmentDocIsCurrent`, `TestNoPackageRedeclaresADefault`) — this PR also **fixes** `TestTheDocumentationListsEverySetting` and keeps `TestEffectExemptionsOnlyShrink` green via the pin raise above. 🤖 queue worker (repo-worker-code), lane E, task 3234 --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Execution output is now capped at 64 KiB by default. When output exceeds the limit, the returned text ends at a UTF-8-safe boundary and includes a marker showing how many bytes were kept, the total size, and how many were dropped. The result also indicates that stdout was truncated. * Configure the limit with `exec.maxOutputBytes`; set it to `0` to disable truncation. The setting applies to both daemon and local execution. * Full output remains available to processing and hooks, and is unchanged in existing run records and artifacts.
